75: 
76: When appending Spec Kit hooks, preserve existing Superset `notify.sh`
77: entries. Multiple hooks for one event run concurrently, so hook commands must be
78: idempotent and must not rely on registration order.
79: 
80: ### 3.1 Tool-Level Guard Adapters (Claude / OpenCode parity)
81: 
82: Beyond the session-lifecycle hooks, Codex mirrors the repo's guard hooks as thin
83: adapters over the same runtime-neutral cores the Claude hooks and OpenCode plugins
84: use. Each fails open (exit 0 on empty/malformed stdin); the two deny-capable guards
85: emit `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: "deny"`, which Codex honors.
86: 
87: | Event · matcher | Guard | Adapter |
88: |---|---|---|
89: | PreToolUse · `exec\|Bash\|apply_patch\|edit` | spec-gate enforce (deny-capable) | `system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/spec-gate-enforce.mjs` |
90: | UserPromptSubmit | spec-gate classify (state only, no emit) | `system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/spec-gate-classify.mjs` |
91: | PreToolUse · `exec\|Bash` | dispatch preflight lint (deny-capable) | `.skilled/hooks/dispatch/codex/dispatch-preflight-lint.mjs` |
92: | PostToolUse · `apply_patch\|edit` | post-edit quality | `.skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/codex/post-edit-quality.cjs` |
93: | PostToolUse · `exec\|Bash` | dispatch audit (observe) | `.skilled/hooks/dispatch/codex/dispatch-audit-posttooluse.mjs` |
94: | Stop | completion-evidence sentinel (advisory) | `system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/completion-evidence-stop.cjs` |
95: | PreToolUse · `mcp__.*` | mcp route guard (dormant until an external MCP family registers) | `.skilled/hooks/mcp-route-guard/codex/mcp-route-guard.cjs` |
96: 
97: > Codex delivers an `apply_patch` target path inside `tool_input.command` (the
98: > `*** Add/Update/Delete File:` header), not a `file_path` field — filePath-driven
99: > adapters parse the path from the patch body. A Stop hook's stdout is parsed as a
100: > response envelope, so neutral shell scripts wired to Stop must not emit stdout.
101: 
102: > Codex 0.160 renamed its shell tool from `exec` to `Bash`, and a matcher of
103: > `exec` alone no longer fires for a shell call. Every shell matcher names both.
104: > The same release hands PostToolUse the shell output as one string where older
105: > builds handed `{stdout, stderr}`, so the audit adapter reads either shape.
106: 
107: > Codex runs a project hook only after the operator approves that exact entry.
108: > The approval is stored in `~/.codex/config.toml` under `[hooks.state."..."]` as a
109: > `trusted_hash`, and an entry with no approval is skipped without a warning. Because
110: > the approval is a hash, a changed entry is likely to need approving again. After a
111: > `hooks.json` change, open `/hooks` in an interactive Codex session and approve every
112: > entry it lists as needing review.
113: 
114: > Codex has no task-dispatch guard. Its `spawn_agent` call reaches PreToolUse as
115: > `collaborationspawn_agent`, but the hook payload carries the spawn `message`
116: > encrypted (`gAAAAA...`) beside `task_name` and `fork_turns`, so the guard has no
117: > prompt or target to check.
118: 
119: Codex loads the full repo hook set (lifecycle and guards) from `.codex/hooks.json`.
120: The user-global `~/.codex/hooks.json` must hold no copy of it, or every hook runs
121: twice. `.skilled/bin/install-codex-hooks.mjs` removes such copies, backs up first,
122: and keeps Superset and other third-party entries.
123: 
124: ---
125: 
126: ## 4. EVENT INPUTS
127: 
128: Hook commands receive JSON on stdin. Current generated schemas use snake_case
129: field names and reject unknown properties.
130: 
131: `SessionStart` required shape:
132: 
133: ```json
134: {
135:   "session_id": "uuid",
136:   "transcript_path": null,
137:   "cwd": "/workspace",
138:   "hook_event_name": "SessionStart",
139:   "model": "gpt-5.5",
140:   "permission_mode": "default",
141:   "source": "startup"
142: }
143: ```
144: 
145: `source` is `startup`, `resume`, or `clear`.
146: 
147: `UserPromptSubmit` adds turn-scoped prompt fields:
148: 
149: ```json
150: {
151:   "session_id": "uuid",
152:   "turn_id": "uuid",
153:   "transcript_path": null,
154:   "cwd": "/workspace",
155:   "hook_event_name": "UserPromptSubmit",
156:   "model": "gpt-5.5",
157:   "permission_mode": "default",
158:   "prompt": "user prompt"
159: }
160: ```
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 5. EVENT OUTPUTS
165: 
166: Use JSON output for model-visible context:
167: 
168: ```json
169: {
170:   "hookSpecificOutput": {
171:     "hookEventName": "UserPromptSubmit",
172:     "additionalContext": "Advisor: live; use sk-code 0.91/0.23 pass."
173:   }
174: }
175: ```
176: 
177: For `SessionStart`, set `"hookEventName": "SessionStart"` and put startup
178: context in `additionalContext`.
179: 
180: Codex also accepts plain stdout for context on injecting events, but JSON is the
181: preferred Spec Kit path because it is explicit and testable. Context is recorded
182: as a developer-role message in the conversation state. For `SessionStart`, it is
183: placed before the first user prompt; for `UserPromptSubmit`, it is placed after
184: the submitted user message.
185: 
186: ---
187: 
188: ## 6. EXIT AND TIMEOUT SEMANTICS
189: 
190: | Condition | Behavior |
191: | --- | --- |
192: | Exit `0` | Success. Output is parsed and injected when `additionalContext` is present. |
193: | `UserPromptSubmit` exit `2` with stderr | Blocks the turn; stderr becomes the reason. |
194: | Other non-zero exits | Fail-open. Codex logs the hook failure and continues the turn. |
195: | Timeout | Fail-open. Default is 600 seconds unless `timeout` / `timeoutSec` is set. |
196: 
197: Spec Kit hooks use short per-hook timeouts in registration and return `{}` on
198: fail-open paths. The prompt hook emits a bounded stale advisory on cold-start
199: timeout so the user can see the advisor surface is installed.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 7. SPEC KIT HOOK WIRING
204: 
205: Installed paths:
206: 
207: - `SessionStart`: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/dist/hooks/codex/session-start.js`

209:

214:   | node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/dist/hooks/codex/session-start.js
215: ```

221: 
222: Expected stdout is `{}` or a JSON object with
223: `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`; for matching work prompts it should be
224: non-empty and start with `Advisor:` on the prompt hook.
225: 
226: ---

681: 
682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |

124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |

134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231:

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073:

# Codex CLI - Complete Command Reference

Comprehensive reference for all Codex CLI commands, flags, models, configuration, and troubleshooting.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Core Principle

Codex CLI is OpenAI's terminal-based AI coding agent powered by `gpt-5.5` — a balanced model used across code generation, review, architecture analysis, and research. The skill dispatches `gpt-5.5` at `medium` reasoning on the `fast` service tier by default; users can override reasoning effort (e.g. "Use gpt 5.5 high fast"). It provides direct access to OpenAI's capabilities from the command line, including code generation, file manipulation, shell execution, web browsing, and multi-turn sessions — all governed by configurable sandbox modes.

### Purpose

Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Codex CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, sandbox modes, and troubleshooting guidance.

### When to Use

- Setting up or configuring Codex CLI
- Looking up command-line flags, subcommands, or agent configurations
- Troubleshooting authentication, sandbox, or session issues
- Configuring agents via `.codex/agents/*.toml`
- Selecting the right sandbox mode for a task

### Key Sources

| Source | URL |
|--------|-----|
| **Repository** | https://github.com/openai/codex |
| **License** | MIT |
| **Runtime** | Node.js 18+ |

---

## 2. INSTALLATION

| Method | Command | Notes |
|--------|---------|-------|
| **npm global** | `npm i -g @openai/codex` | Persistent install, recommended for scripts |
| **Homebrew** | `brew install --cask codex` | macOS-native, auto-updates via `brew upgrade` |
| **Upgrade (npm)** | `npm update -g @openai/codex` | Update to latest version |
| **Upgrade (Homebrew)** | `brew upgrade --cask codex` | Update via Homebrew |

**Platform support:**

| Platform | Status |
|----------|--------|
| macOS | Full support |
| Linux | Full support |
| Windows (WSL) | Experimental — use WSL 2 for best results |

After installation, run `codex` for the full-screen TUI or `codex exec "prompt" --model gpt-5.5` for non-interactive use.

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

cli-opencode applies context-budget semantics to its dispatches. This file records the cli-opencode-specific model windows (§4) and truncation marker syntax (§5), so callers can compose bounded prompts without a second implementation or a drift-prone ruleset.

### When to Use

Consult this reference when composing a bounded cli-opencode prompt and you need the cli-opencode-specific model windows (§4) and truncation marker syntax (§5).

### Core Principle

Keep prompts within the selected model window. Apply the truncation marker and eviction discipline below so callers compose bounded prompts without a drift-prone ruleset.

**Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).

---

## 2. WHY CLI-OPENCODE RECORDS BUDGET SEMANTICS

Prompt packs hit the same failure mode when tool output, conversation history, and working memory exceed the selected model window. cli-opencode records the semantics here so callers can compose bounded prompts without adding a second implementation or drift-prone ruleset.

This reference is documentation-only. It does not add runtime budget logic or mutate memory state.

---

## 3. BUDGET DISCIPLINES

Apply these disciplines when composing a bounded cli-opencode prompt:

- budget percentage and working-memory defaults.
- file summary thresholds.
- fit-to-budget truncation behavior.
- priority eviction order.
- marker interpretation.

The cli-opencode-specific model windows are in §4. The truncation marker syntax is in §5.

---

## 4. CLI-OPENCODE-SPECIFIC NOTES

## 3. HOW IT WORKS

### Prerequisites

Install with `npm i -g @openai/codex`, or with `brew install --cask codex`.
cli-codex authenticates through **ChatGPT OAuth only**. Run `codex login` and complete the browser flow, which requires a ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Edu/Enterprise account. The skill does not use an OpenAI API key.
The ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) holds the full install, auth, flag, sandbox, session and troubleshooting tables. This section keeps only the routing decisions and dispatch-critical gotchas.

### Execution Ownership

This packet owns user-facing routing, the `command -v codex` availability probe, prompt construction, and the self-invocation guard.
Research and review lineages delegate process construction and execution to the already-shipped deep-loop runtime at `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs`, using executor kind `cli-codex`.
That runner accepts only the `research` and `review` loop types, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.

The runtime is the single Codex execution adapter. Do not add a packet-local wrapper, command builder, or spawn path. Direct `codex exec` snippets below are operator reference and manual-testing examples; research and review lineages use the shared runtime, and a one-shot dispatch uses the child envelope.

### Provider Auth Pre-Flight (ChatGPT OAuth)

**MANDATORY before any first dispatch in a session.** cli-codex authenticates through ChatGPT OAuth only. If `codex login` has not been completed on this machine, a dispatch fails with `401 Unauthorized` or `not authenticated` mid-round-trip. Run this check once per session, cache the result, and re-run it only if a dispatch fails with an auth error.

```bash
# One-shot pre-flight: capture ChatGPT OAuth status for routing
CODEX_AUTH=$(codex login status 2>&1)
echo "$CODEX_AUTH" | grep -qi "logged in\|chatgpt-oauth" && CODEX_OAUTH_OK=1 || CODEX_OAUTH_OK=0
```

**Decision tree** (apply in order — first match wins):

| State | CODEX_OAUTH_OK | Action |
|-------|----------------|--------|
| OAuth ready | 1 | Proceed with `codex exec --model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| Not logged in | 0 | **ASK user** to run `codex login` — surface the command, do NOT dispatch. Never substitute an API key or a different model. |

**User prompt template — not logged in:**

```
Codex is not authenticated on this machine. cli-codex uses ChatGPT OAuth only.
Run `codex login` (browser flow; requires a ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Edu/Enterprise account),
then confirm when login finishes — the skill will retry the original dispatch.
```

**Error-recovery contract.** If a dispatch returns an auth error after pre-flight passed (OAuth expired or revoked), invalidate the cache, rerun `codex login`, and re-check before retrying. Never substitute a model the user didn't approve.

### Default Invocation (Skill Default)

**Default model + effort + tier**: `gpt-5.5` · `medium` reasoning · `fast` service tier. Balances speed, cost, and quality for the typical delegation.

> **Fan-out fallback:** a deep-loop lineage that pins no model runs **GPT Luna**. The family is named here on purpose, without a version or an effort tier, so this line does not go stale when the family ships a point release; the runner resolves the current id. A drift test keeps the two in the same family.

```bash
codex exec \
  --model gpt-5.5 \
  -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" \
  -c service_tier="fast" \
  -c approval_policy=never \
  --sandbox workspace-write \
  "<prompt>" </dev/null
```

The trailing `</dev/null` is not optional in a non-interactive dispatch; Rule 6 below explains what a backgrounded codex does to an inherited stdin.

**User override** (honor explicit user phrasing verbatim):

| User says | Resolve to |
|-----------|------------|
| (nothing specified) | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 5.5 high fast" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="high" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 5.5 low" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="low" -c service_tier="fast"` (fast stays unless user drops it) |
| "Use gpt 5.5 xhigh" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="xhigh" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 6 luna max" | `--model gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort="max" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 5.6 terra high" | `--model gpt-5.6-terra -c model_reasoning_effort="high" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 6.1 terra high" | `--model gpt-6.1-terra -c model_reasoning_effort="high" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 6 sol ultra" | `--model gpt-6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort="ultra" -c service_tier="fast"` |

Honor whichever dimensions the user names. Model stays on `gpt-5.5` and service tier stays on `fast` unless the user explicitly names a different model or tier; keep the reasoning effort within the chosen model's ceiling (see Model Selection below and the roster in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md)).

### Model Selection

`gpt-5.5` at `medium` on the `fast` service tier (`-c service_tier="fast"`) is the skill default for cross-AI delegation.
Alternates are `gpt-6-luna` (≤ `max`), and `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-6.1-terra` and `gpt-6-sol` (≤ `ultra`).
[references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md) holds the full roster, the per-model effort ceilings and the 8-level effort ladder.
Set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"`. There is **no `--reasoning-effort` flag**.

**Selection Strategy**: default `gpt-5.5 medium`; raise to `high` / `xhigh` for architecture, security, and complex planning; escalate the model when the task wants reasoning past `xhigh`; drop to `low` / `minimal` for trivial lookups. Per-task rationale table: [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) §5.

### Codex Agent Delegation

The calling AI is the conductor; Codex profiles in `$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml` shape HOW Codex processes the task (sandbox, reasoning). Route with `-p <name>` when the task matches a specialization. Full roster and invocation patterns: [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md).

| Task Type | Profile |
|-----------|---------|
| Code review / security audit | `review` |
| Architecture exploration | `context` |
| Technical research | `research` (+ top-level `--search`) |
| Documentation generation | `write` |
| Fresh-perspective debugging | `debug` |
| Multi-strategy planning | `ai-council` |

Git diff review uses the built-in subcommand (no `-p`): `codex exec review "..." --commit HEAD`. Profiles may override `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode`, `approval_policy`. The `.codex/agents/*.toml` files define personas for the interactive multi-agent TUI, NOT the `-p` flag.

### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas

The full flag glossary, sandbox modes, unique capabilities (`/review`, `--search`, `codex mcp`, session resume/fork, `--image`, `codex cloud`), essential command examples, and troubleshooting table are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Five gotchas that break a dispatch, or make a child misreport its result, and must be honored at routing time:

- **`codex exec` defaults to `--sandbox read-only`** — file-modification tasks silently no-op (the agent plans changes but cannot write them). Pass `--sandbox workspace-write`; for headless no-prompt execution use top-level `-a never` before `exec` or `-c approval_policy=never`.
- **`--search` is a top-level flag, not an `exec` flag.** Enable live web search as `codex --search exec …`, because it precedes the subcommand.
  On codex ≥ 0.144 `codex exec --search` hard-fails with `unexpected argument '--search'`, and older 0.125 builds accepted it, so treat any `exec … --search` example as stale.
  Without it, `codex exec` has no web access and answers from training data only. Every dispatch needing live data (latest versions, repo facts, advisories) MUST use `codex --search exec …`.
- **Always pass `-c service_tier="fast"` explicitly** — this routes through the fast tier instead of whatever the caller's `~/.codex/config.toml` defaults to. Explicit means reproducible regardless of who runs it.
- **No `--reasoning-effort`, `--reasoning`, or `--quiet` flag exists** — set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"`; capture the last message with `-o file.txt`; capture stderr with `2>&1`.
- **`--sandbox workspace-write` blocks local IPC sockets, so a child cannot run checks that start `tsx`.** spec-kit's `npm --prefix runtime/cli run check` fails there with `listen EPERM`, and it also fails with `TMPDIR` pointed elsewhere. It passes outside the sandbox. That was observed 2026-09-24 on codex-cli 0.156.1.
  Tell the child which checks to leave to you, run them in the orchestrating session after it returns, and read that EPERM as a sandbox limit, not a code failure.

    14	# Codex CLI Hook Contract
    15	
    16	---
    17	
    18	## 1. OVERVIEW
    19	
    20	Codex CLI 0.130.0 exposes native hooks behind the stable `hooks` feature flag.
    21	Spec Kit uses the native `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit` surfaces
    22	to inject startup context and the compact skill-advisor brief.
    23	
    24	---
    25	
    26	## 2. ACTIVATION
    27	
    28	Hooks are inert unless enabled:
    29	
    30	```toml
    74	```
    75	
    76	When appending Spec Kit hooks, preserve existing Superset `notify.sh`
    77	entries. Multiple hooks for one event run concurrently, so hook commands must be
    78	idempotent and must not rely on registration order.
    79	
    80	### 3.1 Tool-Level Guard Adapters (Claude / OpenCode parity)
    81	
    82	Beyond the session-lifecycle hooks, Codex mirrors the repo's guard hooks as thin
    83	adapters over the same runtime-neutral cores the Claude hooks and OpenCode plugins
    84	use. Each fails open (exit 0 on empty/malformed stdin); the two deny-capable guards
    85	emit `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: "deny"`, which Codex honors.
    86	
    87	| Event · matcher | Guard | Adapter |
    88	|---|---|---|
    89	| PreToolUse · `exec\|Bash\|apply_patch\|edit` | spec-gate enforce (deny-capable) | `system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/spec-gate-enforce.mjs` |
    90	| UserPromptSubmit | spec-gate classify (state only, no emit) | `system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/spec-gate-classify.mjs` |
    91	| PreToolUse · `exec\|Bash` | dispatch preflight lint (deny-capable) | `.skilled/hooks/dispatch/codex/dispatch-preflight-lint.mjs` |
    92	| PostToolUse · `apply_patch\|edit` | post-edit quality | `.skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/codex/post-edit-quality.cjs` |
    93	| PostToolUse · `exec\|Bash` | dispatch audit (observe) | `.skilled/hooks/dispatch/codex/dispatch-audit-posttooluse.mjs` |
    94	| Stop | completion-evidence sentinel (advisory) | `system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/completion-evidence-stop.cjs` |
    95	| PreToolUse · `mcp__.*` | mcp route guard (dormant until an external MCP family registers) | `.skilled/hooks/mcp-route-guard/codex/mcp-route-guard.cjs` |
    96	
    97	> Codex delivers an `apply_patch` target path inside `tool_input.command` (the
    98	> `*** Add/Update/Delete File:` header), not a `file_path` field — filePath-driven
    99	> adapters parse the path from the patch body. A Stop hook's stdout is parsed as a
   100	> response envelope, so neutral shell scripts wired to Stop must not emit stdout.
   101	
   102	> Codex 0.160 renamed its shell tool from `exec` to `Bash`, and a matcher of
   103	> `exec` alone no longer fires for a shell call. Every shell matcher names both.
   104	> The same release hands PostToolUse the shell output as one string where older
   105	> builds handed `{stdout, stderr}`, so the audit adapter reads either shape.
   106	
   107	> Codex runs a project hook only after the operator approves that exact entry.
   108	> The approval is stored in `~/.codex/config.toml` under `[hooks.state."..."]` as a
   109	> `trusted_hash`, and an entry with no approval is skipped without a warning. Because
   110	> the approval is a hash, a changed entry is likely to need approving again. After a
   111	> `hooks.json` change, open `/hooks` in an interactive Codex session and approve every
   112	> entry it lists as needing review.
   113	
   114	> Codex has no task-dispatch guard. Its `spawn_agent` call reaches PreToolUse as
   115	> `collaborationspawn_agent`, but the hook payload carries the spawn `message`
   116	> encrypted (`gAAAAA...`) beside `task_name` and `fork_turns`, so the guard has no
   117	> prompt or target to check.
   118	
   119	Codex loads the full repo hook set (lifecycle and guards) from `.codex/hooks.json`.
   120	The user-global `~/.codex/hooks.json` must hold no copy of it, or every hook runs
   121	twice. `.skilled/bin/install-codex-hooks.mjs` removes such copies, backs up first,
   122	and keeps Superset and other third-party entries.
   123	
   124	---
   176	
   177	For `SessionStart`, set `"hookEventName": "SessionStart"` and put startup
   178	context in `additionalContext`.
   179	
   180	Codex also accepts plain stdout for context on injecting events, but JSON is the
   181	preferred Spec Kit path because it is explicit and testable. Context is recorded
   182	as a developer-role message in the conversation state. For `SessionStart`, it is
   183	placed before the first user prompt; for `UserPromptSubmit`, it is placed after
   184	the submitted user message.
   185	
   186	---

   229	
   230	- OpenAI Codex source schema:
   231	  `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/hooks/src/schema.rs`

   233	  `https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/16226`
   234	- OpenAI Codex issue evidence for `UserPromptSubmit.additionalContext` becoming
   235	  model-visible developer context:
   236	  `https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/16933`

    25

    27	
    28	Hooks are inert unless enabled:
    29	
    30	```toml
    74	```

    76	When appending Spec Kit hooks, preserve existing Superset `notify.sh`
    77	entries. Multiple hooks for one event run concurrently, so hook commands must be
    78	idempotent and must not rely on registration order.

    81	
    82	Beyond the session-lifecycle hooks, Codex mirrors the repo's guard hooks as thin
    83	adapters over the same runtime-neutral cores the Claude hooks and OpenCode plugins
    84	use. Each fails open (exit 0 on empty/malformed stdin); the two deny-capable guards
    85	emit `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: "deny"`, which Codex honors.

    88	|---|---|---|
    89	| PreToolUse · `exec\|Bash\|apply_patch\|edit` | spec-gate enforce (deny-capable) | `system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/spec-gate-enforce.mjs` |
    90	| UserPromptSubmit | spec-gate classify (state only, no emit) | `system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/spec-gate-classify.mjs` |
    91	| PreToolUse · `exec\|Bash` | dispatch preflight lint (deny-capable) | `.skilled/hooks/dispatch/codex/dispatch-preflight-lint.mjs` |
    92	| PostToolUse · `apply_patch\|edit` | post-edit quality | `.skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/codex/post-edit-quality.cjs` |
    93	| PostToolUse · `exec\|Bash` | dispatch audit (observe) | `.skilled/hooks/dispatch/codex/dispatch-audit-posttooluse.mjs` |
    94	| Stop | completion-evidence sentinel (advisory) | `system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/codex/completion-evidence-stop.cjs` |
    95	| PreToolUse · `mcp__.*` | mcp route guard (dormant until an external MCP family registers) | `.skilled/hooks/mcp-route-guard/codex/mcp-route-guard.cjs` |
    96	
    97	> Codex delivers an `apply_patch` target path inside `tool_input.command` (the
    98	> `*** Add/Update/Delete File:` header), not a `file_path` field — filePath-driven
    99	> adapters parse the path from the patch body. A Stop hook's stdout is parsed as a
   100	> response envelope, so neutral shell scripts wired to Stop must not emit stdout.
   101	
   102	> Codex 0.160 renamed its shell tool from `exec` to `Bash`, and a matcher of
   103	> `exec` alone no longer fires for a shell call. Every shell matcher names both.
   104	> The same release hands PostToolUse the shell output as one string where older
   105	> builds handed `{stdout, stderr}`, so the audit adapter reads either shape.
   106	
   107	> Codex runs a project hook only after the operator approves that exact entry.
   108	> The approval is stored in `~/.codex/config.toml` under `[hooks.state."..."]` as a
   109	> `trusted_hash`, and an entry with no approval is skipped without a warning. Because
   110	> the approval is a hash, a changed entry is likely to need approving again. After a
   111	> `hooks.json` change, open `/hooks` in an interactive Codex session and approve every
   112	> entry it lists as needing review.

   115	> `collaborationspawn_agent`, but the hook payload carries the spawn `message`
   116	> encrypted (`gAAAAA...`) beside `task_name` and `fork_turns`, so the guard has no
   117	> prompt or target to check.

   121	twice. `.skilled/bin/install-codex-hooks.mjs` removes such copies, backs up first,
   122	and keeps Superset and other third-party entries.

   176

   178	context in `additionalContext`.

   181	preferred Spec Kit path because it is explicit and testable. Context is recorded

    17	
    18	Proven patterns for orchestrating Codex CLI from any AI assistant session.
    19	
    20	---
    21	
    22	## 1. OVERVIEW
    23	
    24	### Core Principle
    25	
    26	The calling AI acts as the orchestrator (planner, validator, integrator) while Codex CLI executes targeted tasks. The value comes from combining different model perspectives and leveraging Codex's sandbox-controlled execution, not from redundant work.
    27	
    28	### Purpose
    29	
    30	Each pattern documented here includes the rationale, implementation template, and practical considerations for combining the calling AI with Codex CLI effectively.
    31	
    32	### When to Use
    33	
    34	- You need a second AI perspective on generated code, architecture, or security
    35	- Codex's strengths (sandbox isolation, `xhigh` reasoning, web search via `--search`) complement the calling AI's strengths
    36	- You want to run parallel AI tasks while the calling AI continues working
    37	- Complex workflows benefit from structured, multi-stage generation and validation
    38	- You need controlled file modification with sandbox-enforced safety boundaries
    39	
    40	---
    41	
    42	## 2. GENERATE-REVIEW-FIX CYCLE
   126	
   127	jq '.issues' /tmp/analysis.json
   128	```
   129	
   130	### When to Use
   131	
   132	- Extracting metrics, function signatures, or dependency lists
   133	- Feeding Codex analysis into the calling AI's decision logic
   134	- Building automated pipelines that branch on structured output
   135	
   136	---
   137	
   138	## 4. BACKGROUND EXECUTION
   139	
   140	**Run Codex tasks in parallel while the calling AI continues working.**
   246	**Always pair `codex exec ... &` inside a read-loop with `</dev/null` on the redirection.** This is independent of whether codex itself uses stdin — the issue is shared FD consumption, not a feature.
   247	
   248	### Echoed-Transcript Parsing When Capturing `codex exec` Output
   249	
   250	When you capture a `codex exec` transcript to a file and later parse it for structured output (a fenced JSON block, a verdict line, etc.), remember the transcript contains **three copies** of any marker your prompt mentions: (1) the **echoed prompt** itself — including any output-format template you embedded, with its literal placeholders; (2) the model's streamed answer; (3) the CLI **reprinting the final message** at the end.
   251	
   252	**Symptom:** A parser that extracts text *between* the first and last marker concatenates all three blocks into invalid JSON (so your finding count comes out 0), and a global `grep` for a verdict/status line matches the **instruction line in the echoed prompt** (which usually lists every possible value), so you record the wrong one.
   253	
   254	**Root cause:** `codex exec` echoes the full prompt and reprints its last message; any template token you put in the prompt reappears verbatim in the captured output.
   255	
   256	```bash
   257	# BAD: between-markers awk spans the echoed template + answer + reprint
   258	awk '/^===BLOCK===$/{f=1;next} /^===END===$/{f=0} f{print}' transcript.md   # → invalid JSON
   259	grep -oE 'Verdict: (PASS|FAIL)' transcript.md | tail -1                      # → matches echoed instruction
   260	
   261	# GOOD: collect EVERY fenced block, parse each independently, drop the
   262	# placeholder echo (e.g. severity == "P0|P1|P2"), dedup, derive status from
   263	# what survives. (Reference implementation: the run_review.sh driver under
   264	# specs/.../123-deep-loop-parallel-fanout/008-deep-review/review/.)
   265	```
   266	
   267	**Better still:** have codex write structured output with `-o lastmessage.txt`, or use a unique non-template sentinel the prompt never quotes. And always inspect one real captured transcript before trusting any count derived from it.
   268	
   269	---
   270	
   271	## 5. MODEL SELECTION STRATEGY
   272	
   273	**Codex CLI supports 2 models. Choose based on task type.**
   274	
   275	### Decision Matrix

24	## 1. OVERVIEW
    25	
    26	### Core Principle
    27	One place to answer "which model, which effort, how to dispatch" for cli-codex. This mode is single-provider (OpenAI via ChatGPT OAuth) — the choice space is one provider, five models, and one effort ladder capped per model.
    28	
    29	### When to Use
    30	- Choosing a `--model` for a `codex exec` dispatch
    31	- Mapping a desired reasoning effort onto `-c model_reasoning_effort=` for a given model (and staying under its ceiling)
    32	- Recalling the default model + effort + service tier and the canonical non-interactive invocation shape
    33	
    34	### Scope
    35	This file enumerates the provider/model/effort facts and the dispatch envelope. It does NOT own: the full `codex exec` flag surface, sandbox modes, auth pre-flight, or troubleshooting (see [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md)), the cross-AI orchestration patterns (see [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md)), per-model prompt-craft (see §6), or the fan-out / model-enforcement runtime (see §6).
    36	
    37	### Authority pointers
    38	- Full CLI flags, subcommands, sandbox modes, auth pre-flight, troubleshooting → [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md)
    39	- Dispatch envelope + orchestration patterns + failure-mode traps → [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md)
    40	- Default-invocation contract → [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md)
    41	- Routing, intent map, resource map, loading levels and the self-invocation guard → [../ROUTER.md](../ROUTER.md)
    42	
   100	| `gpt-5.6-terra` | `ultra` | Callable directly; no dedicated profile |
   101	| `gpt-6.1-terra` | `ultra` | Callable directly; no dedicated profile |
   102	| `gpt-6-sol` | `ultra` | `sol-verify` profile pins `xhigh` |
   103	
   104	Selection heuristic: default `gpt-5.5 medium`; raise to `high` / `xhigh` for architecture, security, and complex planning; escalate the model when the task wants reasoning past `xhigh` — `gpt-6-luna max` for implementation, `gpt-6-sol xhigh` / `ultra` for verification and review; drop to `low` / `minimal` for trivial lookups. Effort can also live in `config.toml`, a `[profiles.<name>]` block, or `plan_mode_reasoning_effort` — see [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md) §5.
   105	
   106	---
   107	
   108	## 5. HOW TO INVOKE
   109	
   110	### Canonical dispatch shape
   111	```bash
   112	codex exec --model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="high" "<prompt>"
   113	```
   114	
   115	`codex exec` defaults to `--sandbox read-only`, so file-modification tasks silently no-op unless you add `--sandbox workspace-write` (or `--full-auto`). See [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md).
   116	
   117	### Dispatch envelope (child / detached sessions)
   118	When dispatching as a non-interactive child (spec-gate-neutralized worker), prefix the shared env and terminate stdin:
   126	
   127	- `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` — neutralizes the spec-gate for a bound child worker so it does not stall waiting on an interactive Gate-3 answer, and shares the parent's worktree instead of allocating its own.
   128	- `</dev/null` — REQUIRED when backgrounding `codex exec` inside a `while read … done < file` loop; without it the backgrounded process inherits and drains the loop's stdin, silently dropping most dispatches. See [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md) §4 → "Silent Stdin Consumption".
   129	
   130	### Self-invocation guard
   131	A codex dispatch must not recursively re-enter a session already running inside Codex (detection: `CODEX_SESSION_ID` / any `CODEX_*` env var, `codex` in process ancestry, or `~/.codex/state/<id>/lock`). The guard refuses the dispatch — see [../ROUTER.md](../ROUTER.md) §3 "Self-Invocation Guard".
   132	
   133	### Parallel / fan-out
   134	Multi-lineage parallel dispatch is driven by the shared deep-loop runtime (`fanout-run.cjs`, executor kind `cli-codex`), which lives outside this hub — see §6.
   135	
   136	---
